clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old boy presented with 3-day fever, progressive asthenia and cough over 2 weeks, thoracic urticarial rash, and lower back pain. Initial examination showed fever with no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly. Imaging (thoracic HR-CT on day 3) revealed diffuse pulmonary nodules, mediastinal widening, and lytic bone lesions at dorsal vertebrae, sternum, and costal arch. Bone marrow biopsy showed small, round blue cells consistent with tumor infiltration. Subsequent SPECT and bone biopsy were performed. Final diagnosis of Ewing’s sarcoma with metastatic pulmonary and bone marrow involvement was made based on histopathological and imaging findings.
